llms: Enter a listing price to compare what you keep after fees on eBay, Poshmark, Vinted, Whatnot, Mercari, Fashionphile, and The RealReal. Or choose “This is what I want to make” to calculate what to list it for. Shipping, quantity, eBay promoted listings, The RealReal status, and fee overrides are under More options. askedAs: eBay vs Poshmark vs Vinted vs Whatnot fees
what should I list at to net $X
what will I net selling clothes or a bag
method: Marketplace payouts: the default mode asks for the seller's listing price and shows the estimated amount kept after platform fees and postage. The optional “This is what I want to make” mode works backward to solve the listing price — or the sold price on Fashionphile and The RealReal — that returns at least the target amount. Category, calculation direction, and listing price or target are on the main form. Quantity, buyer shipping, seller shipping, item cost, platform filter, eBay promoted listings percent, The RealReal status, and fee overrides are under More options. Buyer shipping and seller shipping default to $0. Buyer shipping is included in the eBay, Mercari, and Whatnot fee base and is treated as money the seller receives on every platform except Vinted. Vinted US charges sellers no commission (the buyer pays a Vinted fee, usually 5% + $0.70, plus shipping); the seller list price equals the target plus postage the seller pays in target mode. eBay most categories 13.6% of item+shipping up to $7,500 then 2.35%, plus $0.30 (≤$10) or $0.40 (>$10); handbags 15%/9%; jewelry 15%/9%; watches 15%/6.5%/3%; athletic shoes 8% at $150+ with no per-order fee; coins/cards 13.25%. Poshmark $2.95 under $15 else 20%. Whatnot 8% commission on the item (4% coins; TCG/sports/comics 8% on the first $1,500) plus 2.9% + $0.30 processing. Fashionphile 30% consignment on the first $3,000 and 15% above. The RealReal category payout chart uses the status chosen in More options (Trendsetter default; VIP keeps more on items $200+). Mercari 10% of item + buyer shipping. Fashionphile and The RealReal appear for luxury categories only (clothing, handbags, jewelry, watches, sneakers). Vinted appears for every category. Fees change; treat as estimates.

method: Commercial real estate: effective gross income = scheduled rent + other income − vacancy and credit loss. NOI = effective gross income − ordinary operating expenses; debt service, depreciation, income taxes, and capital expenditures are excluded from NOI. The tool also calculates cap rate, unlevered return, cash-on-cash return, DSCR, debt yield, LTV, break-even occupancy, gross rent multiplier, target-cap valuation, loan maturity balance, first-year leveraged ROI, projected sale proceeds, annual IRR, equity multiple, and total ROI. Exit value uses next-year NOI divided by the exit cap rate. Results are underwriting estimates, not an appraisal or investment recommendation.

llms: Price calls, puts, and spreads of up to 4 legs (verticals, straddles, strangles, iron condors, butterflies, calendars, diagonals). Sliders for underlying price or % move, target date, and implied volatility, plus an IV crush preset. Shows option value, P&L, Greeks, breakeven, probability of profit, max profit and loss, a payoff chart, and a price-by-date P&L heat map. American (binomial) and European (Black-Scholes) exercise.
askedAs: what will my option be worth if the stock goes to $X
method: Options: European options (most index options such as SPX, NDX, RUT) use Black-Scholes-Merton with a continuous dividend yield. American options (stocks and ETFs) use a Leisen-Reimer binomial tree with Richardson extrapolation; calls with no dividend use Black-Scholes, which is exact there. Time is in calendar days to a 4:00 p.m. Eastern expiration. Blank implied volatility is solved from the market price. The IV slider sets leg 1 and shifts other legs by the same points. Greeks are per share (theta per calendar day, vega per IV point) and summed into position Greeks. Breakeven, max profit/loss, and probability of profit are measured at the first expiration; probability of profit is risk-neutral and lognormal at the expiring legs' IV. Results are educational estimates, not investment advice.

name: Covered call and cash-secured put calculator
title: Covered call & cash-secured put
summary: Premium, breakeven, return if assigned, annualized yield, downside risk, and expiration outcomes.
description: Calculate net premium, breakeven, maximum profit and loss, return if assigned, annualized return, scenario P&L, expiration payoff, and an IV-based estimate of finishing in the money.
search: covered call cash secured put premium income assignment annualized yield breakeven downside cushion
llms: Calculate net premium, expiration breakeven, maximum profit and loss, return if assigned, annualized premium return, downside cushion, scenario P&L, and an IV-based estimate of finishing in the money.
method: Covered call / cash-secured put: net premium = quoted premium × 100 shares × contracts − entered fees. Covered-call breakeven = share basis − net premium per share − entered dividends per share. Called-away profit = (strike − share basis) × shares + net premium + dividends. Cash-secured-put breakeven = strike − net premium per share; collateral is strike × shares. Scenario P&L uses intrinsic value at expiration. Annualized figures use simple annualization (return × 365 ÷ days) and are not forecasts. The payoff chart compares the strategy with owning the stock alone or buying shares now. The finish-ITM estimate is risk-neutral and lognormal.

title: Expected move

search: expected move implied volatility iv straddle earnings range standard deviation stock price event move
llms: Convert annualized implied volatility and at-the-money call/put prices into one- and two-standard-deviation moves, straight-line and lognormal ranges, a straddle-based estimate, long-straddle breakevens, and a target-move comparison.
method: Expected move: the IV one-standard-deviation approximation is spot × annualized IV × √(calendar days / 365). The tool also shows a straight-line ±2σ range, a lognormal comparison, and an ATM straddle estimate using an editable factor (0.85 default). Full straddle cost is shown separately as the long straddle's approximate expiration breakeven distance. Results estimate magnitude, not direction. A bell curve shades the ±1σ and ±2σ ranges and marks an optional target price.

askedAs: is my storage unit worth it

method: Storage unit: keep cost = cumulative rent (rising by the annual increase every 12 months) + insurance + one-time move-out cost. Sell-and-rebuy cost = replacement cost × (1 + inflation)^(months/12) − net sale proceeds × (1 + cash return)^(months/12). Reports the first month keep cost exceeds sell-and-rebuy cost and the first month cumulative rent exceeds replacement cost.

llms: Compares listing at full price (with a monthly sell probability, price decline per month, holding cost, discounting at the cost of capital, and liquidation of unsold stock after a time limit) against take-it-now offers and liquidation, in present-value dollars. Solves for the monthly sell-through rate needed for waiting to beat the best immediate offer.
askedAs: should I take the lower offer
method: Inventory markdown: a listed option's value = Σ survival × monthly sell chance × net price (declining monthly) discounted at the monthly cost of capital − Σ survival × holding cost (discounted) + unsold probability × net liquidation value at the time limit. Take-it-now options are worth price × (1 − fees) − per-sale cost. Break-even sell-through is solved by bisection.

llms: Works backward from the expected sale price and platform (eBay 13.6% + $0.30/$0.40, Poshmark 20% or $2.95, Mercari 10%, Whatnot 8% + 2.9% + $0.30, Etsy 6.5% + 3% + $0.25 + $0.20, Vinted 0%, or custom) to the maximum purchase price that hits a return-on-cost, margin, or dollar-profit target after shipping, supplies, promoted listing, returns allowance, sales tax, and time. method: Max buy price: net = buyer pays − platform fees − promoted-listing fee − shipping label − supplies − returns allowance − time value. Max cost = net ÷ (1 + ROI) for a return target, net − margin × price for a margin target, or net − dollar target. Max price before tax = max cost ÷ (1 + sales tax).
